topics.topic: Semantics and mechanism of pre-export legacy Room name correction
questions: Is correcting a legacy room name before export an explicit exception to the rule that a Room is never renamed, and what owner action performs that correction on the VPS?

Does the pre-export correction rename the existing Room while preserving its room_id, replace it with a newly minted Room, or alter only the migration export; and which product action or migration tool performs that change despite the rule that a room is never renamed or removed?
Is the pre-export correction an explicit exception that renames an existing Room while preserving its room_id, or does the rule that a Room is never renamed also prohibit this correction?
What product action changes the room name, and does it change the persisted VPS Room or only the value placed in the migration export?

quotes: A room is created in a project and listed; it is never renamed or removed.

The owner makes the export of a source with a one-time migration script run on
that source's host. The script is not a Registry operation: production Registry
gains no export action, and the source keeps none after the migration.

The import
renames no room: it stores a picked project's rooms under the names the v1
instance gave them (A16), and a room is never renamed or removed afterwards
(R0-10). So the owner, before making the export on the VPS (R0-72), corrects
there every room name of the projects to be picked that breaks this rule
(owner, 2026-11-23, State 0 round-59 T1). The import then copies names the
owner has already checked; it writes no name of its own and refuses none.
judgement.divergence: One implementation provides a source-side owner action that renames the persisted legacy Room before export; another requires an out-of-band edit of the VPS store before running the export script. The owner notices which correction workflow exists and whether it is governed by a product action.
judgement.why: The texts require correction on the VPS before export and distinguish it from import-time renaming, but do not identify the action that changes the legacy Room or expressly delimit how that source-side change relates to the general no-rename rule.

outcomes: The owner uses a defined source-product action that renames the persisted legacy Room before export.
The owner edits the legacy store out of band because no source-product rename action exists; the export then reads the edited name.

topics.topic: Creator and name-writer provenance for Rooms stored by import
questions: Who creates the production Room record when the import stores a picked project's existing rooms: the import itself, the owner, or Kernel?

For a Room stored by the import, who creates the production Room record and who counts as the writer of its name: the owner confirming the import, the import or migration closure, the source Registry, or the actor who last changed the source name?

and the request id of its create, as the caller gave it (R0-36; owner,

author_guidance: Before editing, identify the decision's owning state from the phase purpose, question_scope and layer obligations, then choose a disposition for each topic that awaits one.
fixed: repair a decision the owning state must make; do not add later-layer implementation choices merely to close a topic. Record the fix commit and review the changed text once.

carried: name the receiving layer and use --what to preserve the choice, its options and consequences, and the required guarantee every option must keep. Decide any guarantee owned here before carrying its execution onward.
accepted: explain why the remaining choice is permitted. Bring an unresolved product choice to the owner with its options and consequences; absence of a quoted requirement does not decide it.
contradiction and standard_violation take no disposition: repair the offending text in its owning state and review the change. Deterministic transition findings must also close through their checks.
